Previous experience in a pension administration, employee benefits, payroll or similar financial services role.

Strong organizational and time-management skills.

description:
Receptionist/ Administrator

37 hours per week

Permanent

Southampton SSJ&I Service, London Road

Salary Scale: 20 - 21 (£25,947 - £26,305 per annum)

About Us

This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic Charity and Housing Association. The Society of St James (SSJ) has been working in Hampshire for over 50 years, delivering high impact, person-centred, accommodation services to adults and young people experiencing homelessness, problematic substance use and mental health problems. We believe that every person is of worth and we are prepared to take risks to house and support the most at risk and socially excluded members of society.

The Impact You'll Make

As one of the primary faces of the SSJ&I Alcohol and Drug Service, you will set the tone for every individual walking through our doors or reaching out over the phone. Operating with a calm, controlled, and welcoming manner, you will seamlessly guide clients to their appointments, pass queries to duty teams or care coordinators, and serve as a reassuring presence during critical moments in their recovery journey.

Working with a person-centred approach, you will directly support Southampton residents who are ready to make meaningful changes to their lives. By connecting service users to vital interventions-from therapeutic groups to prescribing and needle exchange services-and maintaining strong risk management standards, you will help create a safe environment where individuals feel heard, supported, and empowered to grow.

Through building genuine, trusting relationships with our client base, you will actively contribute to SSJ's core mission. Your everyday interactions will help cultivate a community of continuous growth and development, delivering real, positive change for both our service users and the wider organisation.

Who We're Looking For

Engaging & Personable: An innovative, tenacious individual who can connect meaningfully with service users and multitask effectively in a busy reception environment.

Empathetic & Resilient: Someone equipped with a self-reflective, motivated mindset who thrives both independently and as part of a collaborative team.

Flexible Team Member: A dedicated professional ready to work service-based across a 37-hour week, Monday - Friday working week.

Essential Qualities and Skills

Sector Knowledge & Experience: Experience working with this client group and a strong understanding of the impact of substance misuse on individuals, families, and communities. (Transferable skills from working with other disadvantaged groups will also be considered.)

Awareness of Resources: Up-to-date awareness of the issues this client group presents with, as well as knowledge of the relevant interventions, resources, and agencies available locally.

Core Competencies: Strong IT system skills, excellent multitasking capabilities, and proven expertise in risk management and building trusting relationships.

What we can offer you

We value and recognise our staff, offering some generous benefits, as well as the satisfaction of helping people at risk:
- A competitive annual leave entitlement of 25 days rising to 30 days, plus public holidays
- Flexible working options
- Buying additional annual leave
- Comprehensive induction and training
- Counselling, financial, personal support and health and wellbeing services via our Employee Assistance Programme
- Company cycle to work scheme
- Discounted laptops and computers with Jamie's Computers
- Electric Car Scheme
- Blue Light Card

SSJ are an equal opportunity employer and we encourage applicants from all backgrounds and walks of life.

At SSJ, we recognise the benefits of a supported workplace. SSJ is affiliated with Unite the Union. To learn more about their membership benefits or to sign up, you can visit their official website.

For an informal discussion about the role please contact us.

Application closing date: 5pm on Thursday 24th September 2026

Interview date: Wednesday 1st October 2026

Due to the high number of expected applicants, we do reserve the right to close this vacancy earlier.

Should you not hear from us within 14 days of the closing date, please assume you have been unsuccessful on this occasion.

Proven experience working within SEND/EHCP processes, ideally within a post-16, Further Education, or similar setting

Local Government Pension Scheme

title: Administrator
description: Island City Practice is looking for a motivated, organised, and detail-focused individual to join our team in a varied and rewarding administrative support role. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, you will provide comprehensive secretarial, administrative, and data management support, helping to ensure the smooth and efficient delivery of high-quality patient care. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and a commitment to delivering excellent patient support. In return, you will join a friendly and supportive team dedicated to providing outstanding care to our local community. Post details - 32 hours a week Monday: 09:00 - 17:00 Tuesday: 09:00 - 17:00 Wednesday: 09:00 - 18:00 Thursday: 09:00 - 18:00 Friday: Non-working day The role involves processing electronic and paper-based information accurately and in a timely manner, coding clinical information within patient records, and maintaining high standards of data quality in line with practice policies and procedures. You will liaise regularly with clinicians, administrative colleagues, and external healthcare providers, including secondary care and community services, using systems such as the Electronic Referral Service (ERS). The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator. From time to time, additional duties may be required to support the needs of the practice, depending on workload and staffing requirements. Accurately code clinical information using SystmOne. Extract, interpret, and enter information from clinical correspondence and secondary care communications into patients' electronic health records. Process and code clinical results, ensuring all relevant information is recorded appropriately. Summarise patient records and manage the receipt and electronic integration of new patient notes. Maintain high standards of data quality and contribute to data quality improvement initiatives. Process patient referrals to external healthcare providers, including secondary care services, using the Electronic Referral Service (e-RS). Manage urgent referrals, Two Week Wait referrals, and Advice and Guidance requests, ensuring clinicians are kept informed and patient records are updated accordingly. Review, scan, code, and action incoming clinical and administrative correspondence in line with practice protocols. Liaise with patients and external organisations where required to support the efficient completion of referrals. Provide comprehensive administrative and secretarial support to the multidisciplinary team. Process incoming and outgoing mail, prepare correspondence, and undertake photocopying and document management tasks as required. Respond to administrative queries, perform system searches, and support clinical staff with a range of administrative duties. Manage the practice's general email inbox, prioritising, responding to, and distributing correspondence appropriately. Provide reception support during periods of staff absence or increased operational demand, as directed by management. Process requests for private services and medical reports in accordance with practice procedures. Handle incoming and outgoing telephone calls professionally, courteously, and compassionately, resolving queries or directing them to the appropriate person where necessary. Act as a key point of contact between the practice and external organisations, supporting issue resolution and service coordination. Support the effective use of the clinical system by undertaking searches, audits, recalls, and data collection activities. Configure, run, and interpret searches to support clinical audits, performance monitoring, and reporting requirements. Process patient online service applications, ensuring compliance with information governance and data security standards. Collate, validate, and submit data for internal and external reporting purposes as required. Participate in training, team meetings, and development activities to maintain and enhance skills and knowledge. Support colleagues with troubleshooting clinical system issues and contribute to the implementation of new technologies and system improvements. Assist in the development and refinement of administrative processes to improve efficiency and service delivery. Manage the practice's death notification protocol with sensitivity and professionalism, ensuring timely communication with the Medical Examiner's Office. Work in accordance with practice policies, procedures, and confidentiality requirements. Maintain a professional and patient-centred approach at all times. Undertake any other duties appropriate to the role as requested by the Management Team.
